conceptual assets.concept: Architectural register values stored in the register file and presented on rs1_o/rs2_o/rs3_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements storage and readback of architectural registers in reg_file and exposes read values on the rs?_o outputs. In the non-RST_EN generate branch the clocked process writes reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(opa_addr(addr_bits_c-1 downto 0)))) <= rd_i when rf_we = '1' and then assigns rs1_o <= reg_file(...) and rs2_o <= reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rs2(addr_bits_c-1 downto 0)))); in the RST_EN generate branch per-register processes perform reg_file(i) <= rd_i under the decoded condition (unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rd(...)) = to_unsigned(i, addr_bits_c) and ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1') and the rf_read process assigns rs1_o/rs2_o <= reg_file(...). When RS3_EN is active the rs3_read process assigns rs3_o <= reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(rs3_addr(addr_bits_c-1 downto 0)))); otherwise rs3_o is driven to zeros. These RTL facts establish that reg_file holds the architectural register values and rs1_o/rs2_o/rs3_o are the entity exits; corruption of reg_file contents or the stored values would make reads/outputs incorrect, establishing an Integrity objective.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file write decision and target address (which register is updated and when)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements the per-cycle decision and target for register updates. In the non-RST_EN branch rf_we is computed as rf_we <= (ctrl_i.rf_wb_en and (not rd_zero)) or ctrl_i.rf_zero_we and opa_addr is computed (opa_addr <= "00000" when (ctrl_i.rf_zero_we = '1') else ctrl_i.rf_rd when (ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1') else ctrl_i.rf_rs1); the clocked process uses rf_we and opa_addr to perform reg_file(...) <= rd_i. In the RST_EN branch each per-register process writes reg_file(i) <= rd_i under the decoded condition (unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rd(...)) = to_unsigned(i, addr_bits_c) and ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1'). These RTL expressions define the write-eligibility and the write target; incorrect modification of the computed gate or address would cause updates to the wrong register, breaking the implemented update semantics (Integrity).

The RTL explicitly implements register-0 semantics: in the RST_EN branch reg_file(0) <= (others => '0'); in the non-RST_EN branch rd_zero is computed (rd_zero <= '1' when (ctrl_i.rf_rd = "00000") else '0') and rf_we uses rd_zero and ctrl_i.rf_zero_we so ordinary writes are suppressed for rd_zero unless ctrl_i.rf_zero_we = '1'; opa_addr is forced to "00000" when ctrl_i.rf_zero_we = '1'. These explicit assignments and predicates implement that register 0 is held/read as zero and is write-protected except when ctrl_i.rf_zero_we permits it; violating or bypassing this RTL invariant corrupts the implemented register-0 behavior (Integrity).
